newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MinFins edge up on short positions covering.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFins edge up on short positions covering.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged up on Tuesday in thin trading as investors closed short positions which they opened in the last two days, dealers said.
They forecast range-bound trading in the next few days before any significant news moves the market either way.
"The market is up a tiny bit as many people went into short positions during the fall in the last two days and now they are buying," said Raiffeisen Bank dealer Alexander Chernyatin.
ING-Barings dealer Maxim Arkhipov estimated the market was up by 0.2 percentage points on between $20 and $30 million in volume.

"Range-bound trading will remain for the rest of the week," he said. "We are stuck between two levels and it takes news on the Vnesh debt, (Russian credit) rating or a move in U.S. Treasuries to kick us out of it."
Chernyatin said the market was waiting for the U.S. Production Price Index to be released on August 13.
The PPI will be particularly closely watched after U.S. July payrolls turned out to be higher than expected, he said.
On August 14 the year-on-year and July Consumer Price Index will be released.
Chernyatin forecast the market would sink ahead of the figures, signalling an opportunity to buy on weakness for some investors on a market short of paper.
Arkhipov said tranche 4 was the gain-leader of the day as investors saw it as one of the most attractive investment products due to its high spread over U.S. Treasuries.
The tranche is currently priced at 419 basis points, compared to a 274 bp spread of tranche 3, he said.
